title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation, Salt Lake City and Ogden
description: Wasatch Front suppliers: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 NDT audit files prepared and reviewed for your Responsible Level 3. Share your audit scope with us.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap Audit Documentation for Salt Lake City and Ogden Aerospace Suppliers
html:
Composite, casting, engine-component and defense suppliers along the Wasatch Front, from Ogden and Hill Air Force Base down through Salt Lake City, can use this page to prepare NDT records for a Nadcap assessment or a prime's audit. Atlantis NDT offers ASNT NDT Level III consulting to get those records in order. The NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 documents we prepare and review are approved, edited or rejected by your Responsible Level 3, never by us. Share your audit scope and we reply within one business day.

What Atlantis will and will not do for a Utah supplier

NAS 410 is built around employer certification. Your company issues each NDT certification under its own written practice, and a Responsible Level 3, appointed in writing by the employer, holds authority over that practice, the training, the examinations and any outside agency. Atlantis is not, and will not be appointed as, your Responsible Level 3. No inspector receives a NAS 410 certification from Atlantis, and nobody sits a NAS 410 course or examination with us either. Those limits protect you as much as us: an auditor expects a company representative to explain and defend the program, and a consultant cannot do that on your behalf.

Our work is the groundwork. One of our Level IIIs holds your documents up against the Revision 6 text, the assessor's AC7114 checklists for each method you run, and the specifications on your customers' purchase orders. We list the gaps, draft documents in your format, tidy personnel files, rehearse the audit and help gather corrective-action evidence after findings. Every output goes to your Responsible Level 3 for decision. The national service, with the full list of documents, is described on the NAS 410 audit compliance documentation page.

Utah's aerospace corridor, Ogden to Salt Lake

Hill Air Force Base anchors the industry. The Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity places it roughly thirty miles north of Salt Lake City and describes it as home to the F-35 Lightning II program, with the Falcon Hill Aerospace Research Park beside it as one of the largest enhanced use lease projects in the Air Force. Ogden City's aerospace profile puts employment on the base at about 27,650 people.

The same state office names Boeing, Duncan Aviation, Janicki, Lockheed Martin, L3Harris and Northrop Grumman among Utah's aerospace and defense companies, and lists the state's capabilities as design, composites manufacturing, software and control systems, testing, and repair and maintenance. Ogden's profile adds a roster of employers near the base, including Parker Hannifin Control Systems, Williams International, PCC Structurals, Petersen Inc., Barnes, JBT Aerotech and Northrop Grumman, alongside small machine shops with a handful of staff. Dugway Proving Ground and Utah State University round out the defense and research side.

For NDT, that list means variety. One corridor holds composite structure, castings, engine and control hardware, heavy fabrication and military sustainment work. A NAS 410 written practice drafted for one of those businesses rarely fits the shop next door, and auditors notice when a template was borrowed.

Castings and the radiographic interpretation file

Castings bring radiography into a NAS 410 program, and radiographic personnel files are some of the hardest to keep in order. An auditor will look for the interpreter's certification by technique (film, computed radiography or digital detector array), training and experience in that technique, a specific examination that included real images of the shop's own castings, and near-vision records current at the time each image was interpreted. Image quality evidence, density or signal checks, and the technique sheet for each part number follow close behind. Digital radiography has its own Nadcap slash sheet, and the method checklists are summarized on our AC7114 slash checklists page.

Radiographic exposures are outside what Atlantis does in the US, and radiation safety licensing stays with the licensee. What a Level III from Atlantis can do is review the radiographic procedures, technique sheets and interpretation records, and check that the personnel files behind them meet your written practice. Penetrant on castings carries its own load: porosity and shrinkage indications, sensitivity level selection and the process-control trail for every shift. Method background for local teams is on radiographic testing in Salt Lake City and penetrant testing in Salt Lake City.

Composite laminates and automated ultrasonics

The state's emphasis on composites manufacturing shows up on inspection floors as ultrasonic scanning of laminates and bonded assemblies, often on gantry or robotic systems. NAS 410 programs have to decide how these systems relate to certification. Is automated through-transmission a separate technique from manual pulse-echo? Does an operator who loads parts and starts a scan need the same certification as the inspector who evaluates the C-scan? Your written practice answers those questions, and the answers have to match what your customers' specifications expect.

Auditors then test the answers against the floor. They compare the scan parameters in use with the approved technique sheet, check the reference standard's certificate and insert map, and confirm that the person signing the evaluation holds the right certification and level. A Level 1 Limited category can suit a narrowly defined loading-and-scanning role if the scope is written on the certification and respected in practice. Our review covers both the technique sheets and the certification scopes for each scanning system, and corrected drafts go to the Responsible Level 3 for sign-off. How we structure an ultrasonic technique document is shown on the aerospace UT procedure development page. For background, see the aerospace composite inspection guide and ultrasonic testing in Salt Lake City.

Hiring from the military maintenance workforce

A base the size of Hill means a steady stream of people leaving military service with nondestructive inspection backgrounds, from active-duty aircraft maintainers to civilians who worked depot lines. For a Utah supplier, they are an obvious source of experienced inspectors. They also bring a documentation question that a Nadcap assessor will ask about: how did your company decide what their military training and experience were worth?

Military NDI training and hours do not convert automatically into a NAS 410 certification at a civilian employer. Certification starts over at the hiring company, through its written practice. Credit for service training and hours is a judgment for the Responsible Level 3 there, made on documented evidence. Useful evidence includes training transcripts with course content and hours, records of the methods and techniques the person actually performed, supervisor statements of experience, and any prior certification documents the person can lawfully share. The employer still gives its own specific and practical examinations on its own hardware, and a fresh vision examination.

We draft a credit procedure for prior experience that your Responsible Level 3 can approve, and we review recent hires against it so each file shows the decision and the evidence behind it. Our training records and certificates page covers the documents that carry weight, and veterans weighing a move into civilian NDT can read about Atlantis's SNT-TC-1A-based courses on the NDT training in Ogden page. Whether any outside course counts inside a NAS 410 program is your Responsible Level 3's call, not ours.

Defense contracts and the flow-down question

With Hill Air Force Base and a long list of defense contractors nearby, many Utah suppliers receive military work alongside commercial orders. Defense contracts can invoke NAS 410 directly, through a prime's quality clauses, or through a service-specific requirement. A supplier that ships to a commercial prime and a defense prime may face two different interpretations of the same personnel requirement, two specification revisions and two audit teams.

A flow-down matrix keeps this manageable. Each row lists a clause from a customer document, and the next column names the paragraph of your written practice that satisfies it, or flags that nothing does yet. When a new contract arrives, the matrix shows exactly where the program must change. Your Responsible Level 3 approves the matrix with the written practice it supports. The base document itself is the subject of our written practice for aerospace page, and aerospace NDT audit preparation lists what to assemble before an auditor arrives.

Small shops with a contracted Responsible Level 3

A machine shop with ten or twenty people and one penetrant line cannot justify a full-time Level 3. NAS 410 lets such a shop appoint a Responsible Level 3 supplied by an outside agency, and lets outside agencies deliver training or examinations where the written practice says so. The auditor will then ask for the agreement: its scope, the methods covered, how often the Level 3 reviews the program, how examinations are given and graded, and where the records are kept. An email exchange or an invoice does not answer those questions.

Atlantis does not fill that role, but we review outside-agency agreements against NAS 410 and your written practice, and we check that the agency's own qualifications are in your files. In small shops, every file counts: with a roster of three inspectors, one lapsed vision record is a third of the sample. The vision examination records and experience logs pages cover the two records small shops most often let slide.

Revision 6 for Utah programs

AIA released NAS 410 Revision 6 with Accuris in December 2025, clarifying certification requirements and adding Appendix D, which lets Level 2 personnel qualify for the initial Level 3 examination by accumulating points for designated NDT activities. For a region where many shops rely on contracted Level 3s, Appendix D may open a path to growing one in-house, provided the candidate's activities are recorded in the categories your written practice adopts. That choice belongs to the employer and its Responsible Level 3.

The transition should be planned as one change: customer dates and the standard's transition wording set the timing, and the written practice, course outlines and examination banks move together. For the background, read NAS 410 explained and the NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison, which helps staff who also hold ASNT-based certifications for industrial work.

How Atlantis supports suppliers in Utah

Atlantis is based in Houston and Hyderabad and travels to Utah when a task needs someone on site. Gap reviews, drafting and record audits run remotely through your secure file sharing. The site visit covers what cannot be judged from documents: comparing scanner settings and penetrant line records with approved techniques, pulling personnel files the way an assessor would, and running a mock audit with inspector interviews. When findings arrive, our role is root cause and evidence: why the gap happened, and what proves it is closed. Your company writes and owns its response.

Regional pages with more context include NDT consulting in Salt Lake City, aerospace NDT in Salt Lake City and NDT consulting in Utah. For assessor habits, see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness.

What to send us

  • Your written practice and revision log.
  • The Responsible Level 3 appointment and, if the Level 3 is contracted, the outside-agency agreement.
  • Commercial and defense contract clauses or specifications that call for NAS 410 or Nadcap.
  • A list of everyone who performs or signs NDT, showing each person's methods, levels, techniques, certification expiry and last eye examination.
  • Complete files for your newest inspector and for whoever interprets radiographs or C-scans.
  • Technique sheets and reference-standard certificates for your most common parts.
  • Findings and responses from your last audit.

Wasatch Front audit-readiness checklist

  1. The written practice fits your actual product mix, not a borrowed template.
  2. Radiographic interpreters hold certifications for each technique in use, with specific examinations on your own castings.
  3. Automated ultrasonic systems are defined as techniques, and operator scopes are written on certifications.
  4. A flow-down matrix covers every commercial and defense specification on open orders.
  5. Any contracted Responsible Level 3 or outside agency works under a signed agreement with a defined scope.
  6. Vision and color-perception records are current for every inspector, including part-time ones.
  7. Examination papers, keys and practical checklists are on file.
  8. Records are retained as long as the written practice and customers require, as set out in aerospace NDT records retention.

faq.q: Could Atlantis become our contracted Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not take that appointment for any client. If you want a contracted Responsible Level 3, NAS 410 allows one through an outside agency; we can review that agreement and prepare documents for whoever holds the role.

faq.q: Will Atlantis certify our inspectors under NAS 410?
faq.a: No. Your company certifies its inspectors through its own written practice, and Atlantis offers no NAS 410 courses or exams. We check whether each file's evidence would satisfy an auditor.

faq.q: Do you take radiographs of our castings?
faq.a: No. Atlantis performs no radiographic exposures in the United States. A Level III from Atlantis can review your radiographic procedures, technique sheets, interpretation records and the related personnel files.

faq.q: How should we certify operators of automated ultrasonic scanners?
faq.a: Your written practice decides, within NAS 410 and your customers' specifications. Some shops use a Level 1 Limited scope for loading and scanning, with a Level 2 evaluating the data. The scope must appear on the certification and be followed on the floor.

faq.q: Our defense and commercial customers flow down different requirements. How do we handle that?
faq.a: Build a flow-down matrix that maps each customer clause to the written practice paragraph that meets it. Your Responsible Level 3 approves it. We draft and maintain the matrix in your format.

faq.q: We have three inspectors. Is NAS 410 realistic for a shop our size?
faq.a: Yes, if the program is written for your size. A contracted Responsible Level 3, a written practice that covers only your methods and complete files for each person usually works. Small rosters make every file matter.

AIA describes two main changes: clearer certification rules, and Appendix D, under which Level 2 staff earn activity points toward eligibility for the first Level 3 examination. Check the transition wording and your customers' dates. See NAS 410 explained.

faq.q: Do you come to Ogden and Salt Lake City sites?
faq.a: Yes, for file pulls, process checks and the mock audit, with document work done remotely. The company's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad; there is no Utah office.

faq.q: Can you help after Nadcap findings are issued?
faq.a: Yes. We help find causes and gather objective evidence that corrections hold. Your company prepares and submits its response. See aerospace NDT corrective actions.

faq.q: Does Atlantis hold Nadcap accreditation or prime approvals?
faq.a: It holds neither. The certificates Atlantis does hold are for ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 management systems; anything accredited or approved in your audit is yours.
